tagline: Self-hosted Ruby on Rails system for building agents that watch the web and act on events.
description: Huginn lets you build small agents that read the web, listen for events and act on your behalf. Agents create and consume events and pass them along a directed graph. The project calls it a hackable, self-hosted take on IFTTT or Zapier. It is MIT-licensed and the code is a Rails app. The README lists many sources and actions: scrape a page and email when it changes, watch RSS feeds, IMAP mailboxes, webhooks and MQTT topics, post to Slack, Telegram or Twitter, send SMS through Twilio, and call OpenAI-compatible APIs to summarize or classify text. Event payloads can be reshaped with Liquid templates, jq filters or small JavaScript agents, and collected events can be served back out as your own feed or JSON endpoint. To try it, run the official Docker image, which bundles every process in one container. For production the docs point to Docker Compose, which runs the web app and a separate job worker against a MySQL or PostgreSQL database. A single-process image exists for splitting the processes. Packages exist for YunoHost and Unraid. Huginn replaces the trigger-and-action core of Zapier or IFTTT. It does not match their catalogue of ready-made app connectors, so some integrations need an HTTP agent or a custom agent that you configure yourself.
strengths: Agents pass events along a directed graph, so one source can feed several actions.
Inputs include RSS, IMAP, webhooks, MQTT and website scraping.
Event payloads can be reshaped with Liquid templates, jq filters or small JavaScript agents.
Official Docker images in all-in-one and single-process variants, with Compose examples for MySQL and PostgreSQL.
Can republish collected events as feeds or JSON endpoints of your own.
limits: Needs a web process, a background worker and a MySQL or PostgreSQL database; it is heavier than a single binary.
The project runs no hosted service; managed hosting is only offered by sponsors listed in the repository.
Connector list is far shorter than Zapier's; services outside the README list need webhooks or HTTP agents.
Community packages (YunoHost, Unraid) may lag behind releases, per the README.
bestFor: A developer or tinkerer with a small VPS who wants private monitoring and notification workflows without paying per task.
